paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the peace of God isn't something you wait around to feel. It's something you receive when you take your worry to Him. Paul says, "Be anxious for nothing, but in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God." (Philippians 4:6) And he gives the reason right behind it: "The Lord is near." (Philippians 4:5)

So what do you do with a heavy heart and a racing mind? Paul says pray, give thanks, and then fill your head with whatever is true, honorable, right, pure, lovely and admirable. (Philippians 4:8) I spent years in a dark drawer, and let me tell you, what I thought about back there made ALL the difference. Even the church at Philippi had two women, Euodia and Syntyche, who needed to agree with each other in the Lord (Philippians 4:2), so nobody gets a pass on needing this, friend.

And look at where it all lands. Paul says to put into practice what they learned, received, heard and saw, and then promises, "And the God of peace will be with you." (Philippians 4:9) That's the best part. Your peace isn't a feeling you have to cook up by yourself. It comes from God Himself, who stays right there with you, so go ahead and rejoice in the Lord, because it was never about how the day is going.
